question: Can products of the frozen three-radical candidates cancel their good-prime ramification even though each individual candidate is ramified?
gate: For each primitive q_i, remove from its outside-discriminant norm all primes shared with the other outside norms, using repeated gcd with their product. A nonsquare private remainder proves a good prime with odd norm valuation unique to q_i. Primitivity supplies a nonzero valuation of pi(q_i) at a prime above it, while all other candidate classes have zero valuation there. Such private witnesses give independent ramification coordinates.
inputs: Only the immutable three-radical incidence certificate. No exceptional points or rank labels.
failure: A square private remainder is not evidence of unramifiedness. Only witnessed columns contribute to the proved ramification-rank lower bound. Unwitnessed combinations remain UNKNOWN. A full set of witnesses excludes every nonzero word in the candidate span, including products with generic Selmer classes.
